items.title: McClean leaves Derry City after contract dispute
items.description: James McClean says Derry City "will always hold a special place in my heart" after mutually agreeing to terminate his contract with immediate effect.

items.title: All Spanish cup matches suspended after Madrid train collision
items.description: All 24 matches in the Spanish Copa del Rey due to take place on Wednesday are suspended as a mark of respect after more than 30 people were killed in a train crash near Madrid.

items.title: Ref Watch: Arsenal's red card appeal will fail - Dowman was aggressive
items.description: Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card in their shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town will fail.

items.title: 'Relax, I love Kane and Lamine Yamal' - Henry defends his Ballon d'Or hosting
items.description: Former Arsenal forward Thierry Henry responds to criticism of a number of comments he made during Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony and claims they were "jokes".

items.title: Arsenal to appeal against Dowman red card
items.description: Arsenal will appeal against Max Dowman's sending-off during Tuesday's Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwood Town.

items.title: Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks
items.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks at the club's training ground.

items.title: Why did Fleetwood have to lose player for Arsenal penalty shootout?
items.description: Fleetwood Town had to remove a player for their penalty shootout against Arsenal - BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why.

items.title: Arteta explains reaction to Dowman red card amid criticism
items.description: Mikel Arteta has explained his reaction to Max Dowman as the 16-year-old went down the tunnel after being sent off in Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

items.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes have met face to face to clear the air, with both vowing to refocus on turning the club's season around.

items.title: Latte Lath: Carrick never screamed, he knew how to listen
items.description: For Emmanuel Latte Lath, the big moment came within three minutes of his Bundesliga debut for Union Berlin. At the age of 27, it was his first appearance in a major European league. And he scored. "It was like an explosion, the emotion that I had inside."
